source.title: Associated forms: current progress and open problems

accepted.question_text: Given an isolated hypersurface singularity in C^n defined by a holomorphic function F, the Mather-Yau theorem says that the singularity is determined up to biholomorphism by n and the isomorphism class of its Tjurina algebra T_F = C[[z_1, ..., z_n]]/(F, F_{z_1}, ..., F_{z_n}). The open reconstruction problem asks for an explicit, constructive procedure that recovers the singularity itself from the Tjurina algebra. In the homogeneous case treated in this paper, where f is a homogeneous degree-d form with isolated singularity at the origin and T_f = M_f, the question is to describe explicitly how to reconstruct the linear-equivalence class of f from the algebra M_f.
accepted.context_brief: Reconstruction from Tjurina or Milnor algebra

evidence.quote: The proof of the Mather-Yau theorem is not constructive, and it is an important open problem—called the reconstruction problem—to understand explicitly how the singularity is encoded in the corresponding Tjurina algebra.
In this situation, the reconstruction problem was solved in [IK], where we proposed a simple algorithm for extracting the linear equivalence class of the form f from the isomorphism class of Mf.

accepted.question_text: Let X_n^d be the variety of nondegenerate homogeneous degree-d forms f in C[z_1, ..., z_n]_d, and let Φ assign to such an f its associated form in C[e_1, ..., e_n]_{n(d-2)}. For every regular GL_n-invariant function S on X_n^d, does there exist a rational GL_n-invariant function R on C[e_1, ..., e_n]_{n(d-2)} that is defined at every point of Φ(X_n^d) and satisfies R ◦ Φ = S? Equivalently, can every regular invariant of degree-d forms be recovered, on the entire image of the associated-form morphism, from a rational invariant on the target space?
accepted.context_brief: Conjecture 1.1 on invariant recovery via associated forms

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1.1. For every regular GLn-invariant function S on Xd_n there exists a rational GLn-invariant function R on C[e1, . . . , en]n(d−2) defined at all points of the set Φ(Xd_n) ⊂ C[e1, . . . , en]n(d−2) such that R ◦ Φ = S.
We stress that it is the stronger conjecture that is required for solving the reconstruction problem stated in the introduction.

accepted.question_text: For all integers n ≥ 2 and d ≥ 3, prove that both of the following geometric invariant theory conditions hold: (C1) the induced gradient map P∇|_{P X_n^d} from P X_n^d // SL_n to Z_n^{d-1} // SL_n is a closed immersion, meaning it is an isomorphism onto a closed subset of Z_n^{d-1} // SL_n; and (C2) the induced map PΨ from Z_n^{d-1} // SL_n to P(C[e_1, ..., e_n]_{n(d-2)})^{ss} // SL_n is an isomorphism onto a closed subset of an affine open subset of the target quotient.

evidence.quote: (C1) P∇|PXd_n is a closed immersion, i.e., an isomorphism onto a closed subset of Z^{d−1}_n // SLn;
(C2) PΨ is an isomorphism onto a closed subset of an affine open subset of PC[e1, . . . , en]^{ss}_{n(d−2)} // SLn.
Open Problem 3.2. Prove that conditions (C1) and (C2) are satisfied for all n ≥ 2, d ≥ 3.

accepted.question_text: For all integers n ≥ 2 and d ≥ 3, show that the image of the induced gradient map P∇|_{P X_n^d} is normal. Since P∇|_{P X_n^d} is known to be finite and injective, proving normality of its image would imply condition (C1) via Zariski's Main Theorem.

evidence.quote: By Theorem 3.3 and Zariski’s Main Theorem (see [TY, Corollary 17.4.8]), condition (C1) will follow if we establish the normality of the (closed) image of P∇|PXd_n in Z^{d−1}_n // SLn.
Open Problem 3.4. Show that the image of P∇|PXd_n is normal for all n ≥ 2, d ≥ 3.

accepted.question_text: For every n ≥ 2 and d ≥ 3, find a homogeneous SL_n-invariant on the space C[e_1, ..., e_n]_{n(d-2)} whose nonvanishing locus contains U_n^{n(d-2)} as a closed subset. Equivalently, produce an invariant J such that U_n^{n(d-2)} is closed in the complement of the zero locus of J; this would imply condition (C2).
accepted.context_brief: Invariant cutting out the relevant target locus

evidence.quote: Proposition 3.9. Suppose that there exists a homogeneous SLn-invariant J on the space C[e1, . . . , en]n(d−2) such that U^{n(d−2)}_n is a closed subset of the complement to the zero locus of J. Then ... condition (C2) is satisfied.

Open Problem 3.10. Show that for all n ≥ 2, d ≥ 3 one can find a homogeneous SLn-invariant on the space C[e1, . . . , en]n(d−2) such that U^{n(d−2)}_n is a closed subset of the complement to its zero locus.

accepted.question_text: Fix n ≥ 2 and d ≥ 3, and consider the associated-form morphism Φ from degree-d forms to degree n(d-2) forms. Whenever the associated form of some nondegenerate input is again nondegenerate, one can iterate Φ. Is every iterate Φ^k, for every positive integer k, a well-defined rational map? In other words, does repeated application of the associated-form construction always extend rationally for all numbers of iterations?

evidence.quote: This observation leads to the following natural question: Open Problem 3.16. Is the iteration Φ^k a well-defined rational map for all k ∈ N?

accepted.question_text: Let p be the smallest nonnegative integer such that the product Δ^p Φ extends from the nondegenerate locus X_n^d to a regular morphism on the entire space C[z_1, ..., z_n]_d. Compute this integer p in terms of n and d, or at least determine it case by case. This asks for the minimal power of the discriminant needed to regularize the associated-form morphism into a contravariant on all degree-d forms.

evidence.quote: The contravariant Δ^pΦ is rather mysterious with even its most basic properties not having been understood so far. Indeed, the very first question that one encounters is: Open Problem 5.1. Compute the integer p.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist any pair (n, d) for which the minimal integer p making Δ^p Φ regular on the full space of degree-d forms satisfies p > 1? Equivalently, is there an example where multiplying the associated-form morphism by a single power of the discriminant is not enough to remove all poles?
accepted.context_brief: Existence of cases with p greater than one

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.5. Is there an example with p > 1?

trace.notes: Resolved the zbMATH record to the exact-work arXiv PDF 1803.04005 and mapped the paper structure. Open problems are concentrated in the introduction, Section 3, and Section 5.
Captured the introductory reconstruction problem and specialized it to the homogeneous case using the paper's own framing.
Rewrote Conjecture 1.1 into a self-contained invariant-recovery question and retained the requirement that the rational invariant be defined on all of Φ(X_n^d).
Extracted the paper's combined GIT open problem exactly from the stated conditions (C1) and (C2).
Recorded the normality problem as a separate subproblem because the paper explicitly isolates it as sufficient for condition (C1).
Recorded the invariant-existence problem as a separate subproblem because the paper explicitly isolates it as sufficient for condition (C2).
Captured the explicit iteration question for Φ from Section 3.4.
Captured the primary open problem in Section 5 concerning the minimal exponent p regularizing Δ^p Φ.
Captured the explicit subproblem asking whether any example with p > 1 exists.

Kept Conjecture 1.1, the reconstruction problem, the two sufficient-condition subproblems, the iteration question, and the two p-questions as distinct because the paper treats them as different mathematical objectives.
All accepted items have verbatim page-cited evidence and were rewritten to remove dangling references to sections, propositions, or prior notation without adding unsupported claims.
